chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said:

One of our companions wrote a letter to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second, with me, asking him about a man who was immoral with a woman, then he married her after the pregnancy, so she came with a child, and he resembles the creation of Allah most by him. So he wrote by his own handwriting and his seal: The child is for him, he does not inherit.

key_terms.أَشْبَهُ خَلِيقَةِ اللَّهِ: resembles the creation of Allah most
key_terms.فَجَرَ: to be immoral or commit fornication

ai.seo_question: Does a child born from fornication inherit from the father if he marries the mother?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that the child of a man who committed fornication with a woman and subsequently married her belongs to the man ('al-ghayyah'), inheriting from him despite the initial illicit act. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that marriage can establish paternity even after conception through zina, distinguishing it from cases where the child is explicitly 'for the fornicator' but may not inherit in the same manner. The emphasis on the Imam's signature and seal underscores the authoritative nature of this legal determination regarding lineage and inheritance rights.
